card.hook: Here's a photo that almost takes itself: yacht hulls and masts in front, open Red Sea behind, and hardly any clutter. Hurghada Marina is one of the easiest places in town to get a clean shot on your phone.
card.stand_here: Stand at the water's edge at Hurghada Marina, right on the phone icon, and face out across the inner harbour toward the open sea. Let the nearest boats fill the bottom of your frame, with sea and sky above.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for the moored yachts with open water beyond. Go to 0.5x if you want more harbour and sky, or 2x-5x (depending on your phone) to pick out one boat or a bit of its rigging.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line the horizon up with one of them so the sea stays straight.
card.best_time: Early morning is the sweet spot, when the water is still and the light is soft. Evening is a good second choice for reflections and atmosphere, and the lit promenade helps frame the scene at dusk.
card.selfie_here: Try the Hurghada Marina promenade, beside the moored yachts in the inner harbour. Use the front camera (or 0.5x if your phone allows it), and keep the yachts over your shoulder. They make a clean, recognisable backdrop, and the evening lights add atmosphere.
card.rules_and_safety: Ask permission before taking close-ups of individuals or private property, and don't stand in the middle of the walkway blocking people while you shoot. One guide says the marina's gated entrances feel secure for an evening stroll.
card.challenge: Spot a dive boat among the yachts and make it the star of your shot, with the sea behind it.
card.good_to_know: Yachts and dive boats moor here, so you get a bit of local character along with the shiny hulls. The Marina Boulevard promenade runs alongside the harbour. The harbour area is free to visit.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand at the water's edge at Hurghada Marina, right on the phone icon, and face out across the inner harbour toward the open sea. Let the nearest boats fill the bottom of your frame, with sea and sky above.

card.hook: Picture a stingray gliding past the glass while a flamingo poses just down the hall. The Hurghada Grand Aquarium is a gift for your camera roll, and nobody will blame you for taking 40 shots.
card.stand_here: Head for the Hurghada Grand Aquarium in the Magawish area. The phone icon on the map sits right at the aquarium itself, so there's no extra walk. Once inside, face the glass of a bigger tank and rest your phone gently against it.
card.zoom: Stay at 1x for most tanks. Drop to 0.5x in the shark tunnel if space is tight. Try zoom 2x to 5x for a single turtle, ray or bird, but only when the animal is close to the glass (higher zooms depend on your phone).
card.make_it_pop: Tap the animal, then drag the slider a little darker if the water looks washed out.
card.best_time: Pick a quieter part of the day so you get room at the glass. For the animals kept in the open, morning is usually nicer for you and more lively for them.
card.selfie_here: Take your selfie in the glass tunnel with the sharks and rays swimming overhead. Use the front camera, or 0.5x if your phone offers it, to fit them in behind you. The raised walkway to the zoo area is another good one, with the tanks below you and the view over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: Flash isn't allowed because it can disturb the animals, and selfie sticks are off the list too. Floors can be slippery, so wear shoes with a good grip. Check the official site before you go for entry and photo rules.
card.challenge: Catch a shark or ray in the upper third of your frame, with clear water all around it, and keep the phone level using the gridlines.
card.good_to_know: The aquarium opened in January 2015 and is Egypt's largest, and one of the biggest in Africa. It has 24 exhibits and more than 1,200 animals from about 100 species. 'Whale Valley' is based on fossils found in the Western Desert.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Head for the Hurghada Grand Aquarium in the Magawish area. The phone icon on the map sits right at the aquarium itself, so there's no extra walk. Once inside, face the glass of a bigger tank and rest your phone gently against it.

card.hook: There's no grand viewpoint to hunt for at Senzo Mall. You walk up to a big modern frontage on Safaga Road, and that's your backdrop. Easy, relaxed, no scrambling.
card.stand_here: The phone icon on the map is at the mall itself, so there's little or no extra walk. The main entrance may not be exactly at the icon, so look for the main frontage when you arrive. Stand where you get the best view of it, and step back from the building to fit more in.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x for the whole frontage. If you're too close to fit it all in, drop to 0.5x. Use zoom 2x for details of the facade or a neater shot of people with less background.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and line them up with the edges of the building, and hold your phone level so the walls don't lean inwards.
card.best_time: Daylight is simplest for a clear view of the frontage. In the evening, check how the building looks and use night mode if it's dim.
card.selfie_here: Pick a spot where the frontage fills the background behind you. Use the front camera, switch to 0.5x if it's available, and hold your phone a little lower so the building stays over your shoulder.
card.rules_and_safety: It's outside a shopping centre, but check on the ground for any restrictions before you take photos.
card.challenge: Take two shots: a wide one with as much frontage as you can fit, then a close one of the details or your group. Bonus points for the one with the fewest cars in the background.
card.good_to_know: Senzo Mall is a modern shopping centre on Safaga Road in Hurghada 1. It also has an outdoor area called Senzo Avenue, which is used for events. If you plan to go inside, check the mall's public Facebook page or confirm locally first.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: The phone icon on the map is at the mall itself, so there's little or no extra walk. The main entrance may not be exactly at the icon, so look for the main frontage when you arrive. Stand where you get the best view of it, and step back from the building to fit more in.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a specific selfie spot or a spot for a passer-by to photograph the visitor with the mall. The only photo-related remark is a general one on airial.travel (https://airial.travel/attractions/egypt/senzo-mall-yS1bMxge): the mall 'offers a modern backdrop for photos' with no named location. Other pages name outdoor areas without calling them photo spots: 'Senzo Avenue' appears in event listings on the mall's Facebook page (https://www.facebook.com/SenzoMallOfficial/photos), and trips2deal.com (https://trips2deal.com/news/senzo-mall-modern-shopping-center-near-sand-city) describes indoor and outdoor food court seating. Because none of these says it is a good photo spot, I left both selfie fields empty rather than guess. No page states selfie stick or tripod rules, and no page gives a safety point for this mall. Location doubt: the coordinates you gave (27.21393, 33.84000) do not match the mall's listed coordinates on TripAdvisor (27.09571, 33.821976, https://www.tripadvisor.com/Attraction_Review-g297549-d4126331-Reviews-Senzo_Mall-Hurghada_Red_Sea_and_Sinai.html). Other pages give Safaga Road / Village Road in the south of the city, and getoccupi.com lists 35 El Hadaba Rd. Please confirm you are at the right point before using any spot.

card.hook: Picture this: white domes, two slim minarets and a row of bobbing yachts, all lined up across the water like the mosque booked the spot on purpose. That's Al Mina Mosque from Hurghada Marina, and it's easy to see why it's one of the most photographed sights in town.
card.stand_here: Stand on the Hurghada Marina promenade, facing the mosque across the water. The mosque is 206 m to the north-east of you, so face that way and you'll get the domes and minarets with the Red Sea and yachts behind them.
card.zoom: Start at zoom 1x to fit the mosque, water and yachts in together. Then try zoom 2x to 5x (higher zooms depend on your phone) to pick out the domes and minarets. Use zoom 0.5x only if you're up close, because it makes the mosque look small.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on gridlines and line a minaret up with a vertical line so it stands up straight instead of leaning.
card.best_time: Go in late afternoon towards sunset, when the light is warm and the marina feels its most atmospheric. Come back after dark too, when the minarets are lit and stand out against the water.
card.selfie_here: Try the far end of the marina embankment on the promenade, using the front camera. Hold your phone a little higher and check on screen whether the mosque is showing over your shoulder, because nothing we found confirms the angle there. If you're close, zoom 0.5x gets more of the waterfront in, but the mosque will look smaller.
card.ask_someone: Walk to the far end of the marina near the fish market and ask a passer-by to take your photo there, with the fishing boats and water in front and the mosque in view.
card.rules_and_safety: If you go inside the mosque, dress modestly. Photography may be restricted in some areas, so check local information before you go.
card.challenge: Take two shots from the promenade, one wide and one tight on the domes, then see which one you'd actually frame.
card.good_to_know: You don't need to go inside the mosque to get the picture. The promenade is a public waterfront space and, according to one guide, free to walk. For a closer, more head-on view, walk on to the end of the marina by the fish market.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand on the Hurghada Marina promenade, facing the mosque across the water. The mosque is 206 m to the north-east of you, so face that way and you'll get the domes and minarets with the Red Sea and yachts behind them.

card.hook: Here's an honest opinion: the outside of Saint Shenouda is modest, and that's part of its charm. Pale walls, big windows and a calm face make it a quick, easy photo stop in the old part of Hurghada.
card.stand_here: Stand directly in front of the entrance on El-Lewaa Salman Mazhar Street in El Dahar. The phone icon on the map is right at the church entrance, so face the building and take the whole facade from the front.
card.zoom: Start at 1x for a straight, natural view of the facade. If the street is too narrow to fit the whole building, switch to 0.5x. Use 2x or more only for details like the windows or the entrance.
card.make_it_pop: Turn on the gridlines and hold the phone level so the walls match the vertical lines, and if the pale walls look washed out, tap them and slide a little darker.
card.best_time: Morning is your best bet, when the street is quieter and fewer cars wander into your shot.
card.selfie_here: Use the front camera, hold it at arm's length and tilt it just enough to fit the church over your shoulder. If your phone has 0.5x on the front camera, it helps fit more of the building in. Keep it quick and relaxed, since this is a working place of worship.
card.rules_and_safety: This is a working place of worship, so be discreet. Ask before photographing anyone, and don't use flash during services. There may be a security checkpoint at the entrance, which is normal. Opening times can change, so check before you go.
card.challenge: Take one photo with the walls perfectly straight on the gridlines, then walk back toward El-Dahar Square and catch the church coming into view on the right for a second shot.
card.good_to_know: Saint Shenouda Coptic Orthodox Church stands in El Dahar, the old part of Hurghada, and is dedicated to Saint Shenouda. Most visitors find the inside more striking than the outside. Think of this as a short, easy stop rather than a long photo session.
card.stand_here_before_gps_rule: Stand directly in front of the entrance on El-Lewaa Salman Mazhar Street in El Dahar. The phone icon on the map is right at the church entrance, so face the building and take the whole facade from the front.

selfie_research.notes: No page I found names a selfie spot with the church behind the visitor, or a passer-by stand point that frames the whole church, so both fields are empty rather than guessed. The closest named pointer is El-Dahar Square: one guide says that from in front of the Gad restaurant on the square, the church is on your right (https://landioustravel.com/saint-shenouda-coptic-church-hurghada/). That is a walking direction, not a photo spot, so I did not list it. The photography guidance I found concerns the interior, not the exterior: indoor photos are allowed with consideration for worshippers (https://excursionmania.com/ttd/3662/saint-shenouda-coptic-orthodox-church-blg-3662), and flash should be avoided during services (https://airial.travel/attractions/egypt/st-shenouda-coptic-cathedral-7VnPskck). No page mentions selfie sticks or tripods, so the rules list is empty. Coordinates were not checked against any page.
